title: Warsaw, 24 Dec 1627, to the Bishop of Olmütz? (DECODE R1408, ÖStA HHStA)

documents.shelfmark: ÖStA HHStA Staatskanzlei Interiora, Chiffrenschlüssel Kt. 14 Fasc. 20 f. 176 (DECODE R1408)

plaintext.source: DECODE lists it as non-decrypted; no reading found before this one. Clear: the dateline 'Di Varsouia 24 Xbre 1627' and a foot-of-page docket read here as '... Card. Dietrichstein' (the addressee, Italian practice).

transcription.notes: NOTES give 509 tokens as Tomokiyo splits them and 442 after joining letter pairs; the measured 465 counts the space-separated tokens of ct.txt as filed. Image seen 2 Oct 2026 (DECODE IMG_R1408_I6588_P1.png, fetched with the project cookie): two corrections applied in decode.py (line 2 'a 12 o' = code 120; line 10 a missing 29, 'stimato'). DECODE also holds its own transcription (DOC_R1408_D1961_1961.txt, transcriber XL, 2020), which marks one unrecognised symbol as *.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution with the alphabet in plain order on figures 13-33 (odd a-m, even n-z), letter pairs as consonant alternates, two-figure syllables, nulls a/m, and three-figure word codes.
system.notes: distinct_symbols is the measured count in the ciphertext. Ten word codes and {03} {04} {12} glossed from context only.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Figures 12-33 show a monoalphabetic Italian profile; a and m annealed as symbols fall to one vowel, so read as nulls.
5-gram annealing on the numbers alone, six seeds, with and without distinct-core constraint.
Unigram word-segmentation scorer.
5-gram + dictionary coverage annealer converges on one key from random and seeded starts.
Same objective on three shuffled ciphertexts tops out far below the real order.
Converged key is in alphabetical order on odd and even figures, which the annealer could not know.
Letter pairs and rare syllable groups read from all occurrences; word codes glossed from context.

Alternative translation added after a report made while quotations were pulled for Lasry's list: 'confido' (40 23 29 19 16 in ct.txt) carries no accent, so 'mi confido' ('I am confident I gave this Most Serene [Queen] to understand') may be 'mi confidò' ('[you] confided to me that [you] had given ... to understand'), which gives the 'honours' clause its object and makes the one able to confer the canonry, the Bishop, the one who gave the Queen to understand. The figures do not decide it; the existing translation stays, the alternative is on the page, in NOTES and in plaintext.txt.

Code groups revisited for Lasry's quotation: continuous conjectural reading with every group glossed (I), new glosses {03} = poi and {04} = pero, [223][159] = sua promessa; one-part alphabetical order of the three-figure code tested: it would exclude Regina (100), Serenissimi (123), ancora (151) and questa (160) and give 160 cotesta, 159 concessione/cortesia, 120 Cardinale; not decidable (the two-figure syllables are not alphabetical, no value confirmed). Leads: DECODE R1409 (f.178) possible sibling, R1392-R1406 keys, behind login.

DECODE images and documents fetched with the project cookie (targets/bordeaux/decode/cookie.txt) into decode/: R1408 (the letter), R1409 (f. 178, 3 images + DECODE transcription), R1410 (ff. 180-181) and the key records R1392-R1406 (ff. 142-174, 45 images, 8 DECODE key transcriptions).

R1409 tested against the R1408 key: DECODE's transcription (1,328 dot-separated tokens: two-figure 12-37, three-figure 101-195, a few 01-08 and 54-98) decoded with the R1408 alphabet gives gibberish ('ulauraqtobnqt...'), -5.05/char under it-cinquecento order 4 against -2.38 for R1408's own figures under its key, and ranks 67th of 500 random keys over the same figures (similar in la, de-1640s, fr-1600-letters, es-golden-age). Not the same key, and a different system (separated with dots, underlined runs, no letter nulls).

R1409 ciphertext-only: two-figure groups annealed as a free homophonic letter cipher (order-4 LM + unigram KL), Italian and German, against a shuffled control; then every symbol free to be a letter or a common pair. Italian real -2.61 vs shuffled -2.85/char, German degenerate; no readable text. R1409 left unread (outside this target).

Key records R1392-R1406 and R1410 checked for R1408's system (ordered numeric alphabet 13-33 with a/m nulls, codes 100-223): none matches. R1392 German 1592; R1393/1394/1396/1397/1399/1400 French Henri IV-era keys (Biron, Montpensier); R1395 and R1405 Latin graphic-sign keys (Turkish court); R1398 French (f. 153); R1402 'Cyphra in Moscoviam'; R1403 Latin/German Polish key with graphic signs; R1404 alphabet sheet; R1406 German place-name nomenclator 'pro Federico'; R1401 a graphic-sign letter; R1410 a German letter with inserted code numbers. No gloss for any open code.

R1408 image checked against Tomokiyo's transcription: line 2 'a 12 o m' is the code group 120 written 1-2-0 exactly as on line 8 (the clerk's 0 and o are one shape), which removes the hapax {12} and the stray null o; line 10 has a symbol between 26 and 33 (Tomokiyo's double space), read 29 = i, giving 'stimato'; 'Seerenissima' (50 21 zg) confirmed as written; the a-null (tall stem) and the figure 2 (flat base) are distinct, so {03} and {04} are two-figure groups, not 203/204.

[120] now has two contexts, 'fra li altri honori che [120] mi fece in Nicolspurg' and 'tal uolonta di [120]', both fitting the addressee's title; the foot-of-page docket reads '... Card. Dietrichstein', the addressee in Italian practice, confirming the §4 inference. Measured: 442 tokens, 110 nulls, 332 significant, 16 unread (the ten code groups in 14 occurrences plus {03} {04}) = 95.2% of significant tokens read; lm.best_language on the read words: it-modern first.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 426 tokens, 43 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -1.943 per letter; random keys -4.877 (z 6.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.847 (mean -2.871, z 29.6); annealer on the real text -2.505. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R1408 linked to ct.txt (Tomokiyo's transcription) and plaintext.txt (decode.py output with the two image corrections); key_file decode.py, which holds the final key

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): plaintext.txt word-divided text read: both sentences build and translate with word codes open (no key material). Per-document C overturned to B. Claim unchanged.

Verification 3 (v3_below_b): R1408's word-divided text alone scores 0.5 on explicit holes (hole rate 0.163) with the 16 unread code tokens as holes. Demoted to decoded, not read; the key letters stay recovered ciphertext-only, the code groups have no key material. Class read -> not read, method -> not solved, fraction_read 0.952 -> 0.

Method restored: key obtained by an Italian 5-gram and dictionary annealer, confirmed by the key's alphabetical order (key recovered from ciphertext-only); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

outcome.method_basis: An Italian 5-gram plus dictionary annealer converged on a key that turned out to be in plain alphabetical order on odd and even figures, confirmed against shuffled-ciphertext controls; letter pairs and syllables were then read from context in Tomokiyo's transcription. Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by an Italian 5-gram and dictionary annealer, confirmed by the key's alphabetical order; class stays not read, as the text does not read.
outcome.notes: Every spelled word reads; 12 code/small groups (16 tokens) glossed, not read. Addressee from the docket (Card. Dietrichstein); sender unnamed. R1409 is not a sibling (different system, unread).
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py tokens (ct.txt with the two image corrections): 332 non-null tokens, 16 code/small-group tokens counted unread Verification 3, 23 Oct 2026: R1408 demoted to decoded, not read (0.5 on explicit holes with the 16 code tokens as holes); no document reads. gaps.detail: Glossed from context only. No sibling letter in this key and no key in Kt. 14 Fasc. 20 (R1392-R1406, R1410 checked 2 Oct 2026); the Dietrichstein papers (Brno, Moravian Land Archive, G 140) are the next place for a copy of the key or a decipherment.
Two contexts and the docket make it the addressee's title (V.S. Ill.ma / Cardinal Dietrichstein); not read from a key.
Hapax; glossed poi / pero from context.
Image checked: they stand as written inside complete words; read as nulls.

texts.label: R1408, HHStA Chiffrenschlüssel Kt. 14 Fasc. 20 f. 176, 'Di Varsouia 24 Xbre 1627'
texts.summary: An Italian letter written from Warsaw on 24 Dec 1627, most likely to Cardinal Franz von Dietrichstein, Bishop of Olmütz (an inference from the content, supported by a faint docket reading Card. Dietrichstein; nothing in the cipher names sender or addressee): the promised Olmütz canonry for one of the sons of the Polish royal couple has not yet been given; 'these Majesties' want it, and the writer asks that it be done or that he have a prompt answer.
texts.note: Decoded, not read (v3 check 23 Oct 2026): the word-divided text in plaintext.txt (the sweep scored the whole file, 0.561, conjectural version and notes included) scores 0.5 on explicit holes, 0.125 plain, hole rate 0.163, with the twelve unread code groups (16 tokens: [100] [113] [120]x2 [123] [151] [154]x3 [157] [159] [160]x2 [223], {03}, {04}) counted as holes. Every spelled word reads and the sense is clear, but the codes carry the titles, the adverbs and the object of the request, so most of its eight scored stretches have more than one hole in ten words. The filled-in conjectural version is not a reading. Blocker: no key material (no sibling, no key in Kt. 14 Fasc. 20; the Dietrichstein papers at Brno are offline).
